---
# ============================================================
# EXAMPLE 1 - RevealJS slides from a single .qmd file
# BioE Computational Tools 2026, Week 7
#
# Render in Positron with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K, or:
#   quarto render example_slides.qmd
# Then open example_slides.html in a browser.
# Press "S" while viewing for speaker notes, "O" for overview,
# "F" for fullscreen, and "E" for print/export mode.
# ============================================================
title: "My Research in Six Slides"
subtitle: "An example RevealJS deck - open the source next to the result"
author: "Your Name"
institute: "Knight Campus, University of Oregon"
date: today
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: default          # try: simple, serif, moon, solarized, dark
    slide-number: true      # page numbers bottom right
    footer: "BioE Comp Tools - Week 7 example"
    transition: fade        # none, fade, slide, convex, concave, zoom
    incremental: false      # true = ALL lists reveal point by point
    code-line-numbers: true
    chalkboard: false       # true adds a draw-on-slides toolbar (HTML only)
    # embed-resources: true # one self-contained .html file (bigger, portable)
execute:
  echo: true                # slides about code usually SHOW the code
  warning: false
---

## A plain bulleted slide

Every level-2 heading (`##`) starts a new slide. A level-1 heading (`#`)
makes a *section-divider* slide.

-   Text, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, and [links](https://quarto.org)
    work exactly as in any Quarto document
-   So do footnotes[^1], images, tables, and math: $E = mc^2$
-   The YAML header above controls the whole deck - read it!

[^1]: Footnotes collect on a slide at the end.

## Revealing points one at a time

Wrap a list in `::: {.incremental}` to step through it with the arrow key:

::: incremental
-   First this appears...
-   ...then this...
-   ...and finally this. (Set `incremental: true` in the YAML to make
    this the default for every list.)
:::

. . .

Three dots on their own line (`. . .`) pause *anything*, not just lists -
this sentence waited for a keypress.

# Section dividers use `#` {background-color="#1a3a5c"}

## Two-column layouts

:::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Left column** - the syntax is a
`:::: columns` div containing two
`::: {.column width="..."}` divs.

Use columns for text next to a
figure, or two figures side by side.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](example_slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=960}
:::
:::

:::
::::

## Executed code: the figure is made *during* rendering


::: {.cell output-location='slide'}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(610)
t <- seq(0, 10, 0.25)
od <- 1.2 / (1 + exp(-(t - 5))) + rnorm(length(t), sd = 0.02)
plot(t, od, pch = 19, col = "darkorange",
     xlab = "Time (h)", ylab = "OD600", cex.lab = 1.4)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Simulated bacterial growth. The curve regenerates on every render.](example_slides_files/figure-revealjs/fig-growth-1.png){#fig-growth width=960}
:::
:::


`output-location: slide` puts the plot on its *own* slide - also try
`column` or `fragment`.

## Highlighting lines of code

Step through code with `code-line-numbers: "1-2|4|6"` as a chunk option:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="1-2|4|6"}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

stickle <- read_tsv("Stickle_RNAseq.tsv")

stickle |> count(Genotype, Microbiota)
```
:::


Each `|`-separated group is one keypress: packages, then reading, then
counting.

## Tabsets work on slides too

::: panel-tabset
### Figure


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](example_slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=960}
:::
:::


### Code


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hist(rnorm(500), col = "grey80", border = "white",
     main = NULL, xlab = "Simulated values")
```
:::


### Python


::: {.cell}

```{.python .cell-code}
# The same idea in Python (shown, not run - no Jupyter needed to render)
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.hist(np.random.default_rng(1).normal(size=500), color="grey")
plt.show()
```
:::

:::

## Tables, math, and callouts

| Group     | n   | Mean stiffness (kPa) |
|-----------|-----|----------------------|
| Control   | 12  | 3.1                  |
| Treated   | 12  | 8.7                  |

The standard error, $\mathrm{SE} = s/\sqrt{n}$, appears inline; display
math gets its own line:

$$\sigma = E \, \varepsilon$$

::: {.callout-tip}
All five callout types (`note`, `tip`, `warning`, `important`, `caution`)
work on slides - use them sparingly.
:::

## Images, sizing, and fragments

An image is one line of Markdown - local file or URL:

``` markdown
![SEM of the scaffold](images/scaffold.png){width="60%"}
```

::: {.fragment}
Any block with the `.fragment` class appears on a keypress - like this one.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
Fragments can combine effects (`.fade-in-then-semi-out`, `.grow`,
`.strike`, `.highlight-red`, ...).
:::

## Speaker notes and finishing touches {.smaller}

The `{.smaller}` class on this slide's heading shrinks everything to fit;
`{.scrollable}` adds a scrollbar instead.

-   Press **S** now: this slide has hidden speaker notes
-   Press **O** for the slide overview; **F** for fullscreen
-   `quarto render example_slides.qmd --to pptx` makes a PowerPoint from
    the *same source* (simpler layouts survive the trip)

What to explore next: themes, `logo:`, `title-slide-attributes`, and the
[RevealJS documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/).

::: notes
These notes are invisible to the audience - they show in the speaker view
(press S). Put your reminders, timings, and transitions here.
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
